Career and Growth at IBM 1. You get an opportunity to work on your corner of interest, even though you are working on some thing else. How? You can opt for some stretch assignment and explore new skills or work on your choice/interest of skill set. 
2. You get an opportunity to showcase your skills and achievements. How? Lot of paper presentations, patents, Technical events held within IBM 
3. Growth in career is easy at IBM. How ? Lot of Certifications and online courses are available within IBM. Also adapting to new skills and opportunities to implement the same are easy in IBM
4. Employee friendly environment. How? Flexible timings, work from home/remote location options 1. Technical events do happen but the entry to other IBMers is limited due to number constraint. So only a few get a chance to attend these events. We need more such events and should be open to more IBMers.

IBM is what you make of it If you are a go-getter and pro-active about advancing your career, you will climb the ladder. A key to advancement is working cross team and with management several tiers above you.  Most of the time you can pick your hours and work from home, extremely flexible. There is so much entrenched bureaucracy, sometimes it makes you want to scream. There are definitely glass ceilings everywhere and you have to know how to break through them or sidestep them.  Make sure to negotiate a good salary. Every person is different and has a different salary even if you are the same band level. IBM runs on strict margins, so money can be tight and even as a high performer you often wonder if you'll be cut in the next round of layoffs.

Good company with long history, but some concerns for future direction Given the size and breadth of the company, there are many opportunities for career growth. Generally well-respected company at least gets you a foot in the door with clients. Constantly re-inventing itself to stay relevant and ahead of the curve. Flexible work options (e.g., work from home) although this is changing and shifting to greater emphasis on physically being in the same office with your team. Constantly re-inventing itself means frequent churn, in some area more than others. Quick to cut funding (marketing, projects, etc.) in order to make quarterly targets. Along the same lines, there are many jobs pushed offshore which can cause unease -- and goes against the push to have teams co-located.
